![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13945275/assets/760ddc657e8372a3860e2553e4f2b713a8b12544586c708e5f2c1922462567a8.png)

On which of the following intervals is the function $y=f(x)$ above continuous? You may assume that all points of discontinuity of $f(x)$ are shown in the diagram.
questions.worked_solution:
To determine the intervals of continuity of a function, we take the domain of the function and exclude any points of discontinuity.

The function is defined on the intervals $(-\infty ,3),$  and $(3,\infty ).$ There is a discontinuity at $x=3$  but this is already excluded.  

There is also a discontinuity at $x=-3,$ so we need to exclude that.

Therefore, the function is continuous on the intervals $(-\infty ,-3),$ $(-3,3),$  and $(3,\infty ).$ It is also continuous on any subinterval of these intervals. 

Among the answer choices, the correct one is the following:

$\,$ $(-2,3)$ 

Notice that:

- $(-3,4)$ and $(0,5)$ contain the excluded point $x=3,$ so the function is not continuous on these intervals.

- $(-\infty ,-2)$ and  $(-\infty ,0)$ contain the point of discontinuity $x=-3$, so the function is not continuous on these intervals.

questions.problem: Which of the following functions is continuous on the interval $[-1,2]?$
questions.worked_solution:
The correct answer is the following. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13945275/assets/e57af2e43bd292195f617f60ffed8055891531a2ca5d0249706497d7932d6639.png)

      

Indeed, this function is continuous on the open intervals $(-\infty ,2)$ and $(2,\infty ).$

Additionally, the function is left-continuous at $x=2.$ Hence, it is continuous on the interval $(-\infty ,2].$

So, we can say that the function is continuous on the intervals $(-\infty ,2]$ and  $(2,\infty ).$ It is also continuous on any subinterval of these intervals.

Therefore, this function is continuous on $[-1,2],$ because $[-1,2]$ is contained inside the interval $(-\infty ,2].$

Notice that:

- $g(x)$ and $p(x)$ are not left-continuous at $x=2.$

- $h(x)$ is not defined at $x=-1,$ and so it is not continuous on the interval $[-1,2].$

- $q(x)$ is not defined at $x=1,$ and so it is not continuous on the interval $[-1,2].$

- The function is *not* continuous on $[4,\infty ).$ Although the function is continuous on $(4,\infty ),$ it is not right-continuous at $x=4.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."
